frequency_question: How often do major contested federal regulations successfully reach final publication in the Federal Register without being permanently blocked or abandoned due to structural friction within a tight timeframe?
membership_rule: Includes rules designated as economically significant (e.g., impact > $100M) that faced major procedural, interagency, or judicial friction during the rulemaking lifecycle. Excludes non-controversial routine updates and emergency interim rules without public notice periods.

cases.name: EPA Clean Power Plan Replacement / ACE (2019)

coverage_note: 10 named prominent cases; representative of highly contested, high-stakes federal rulemakings facing intense friction.
known_gaps: Selection bias toward the most heavily litigated rules; lower-profile administrative frictions may have higher completion rates.
skeleton: 10 major contested rules examined; 4 successfully reached final implementation despite severe structural and legal friction, while 6 were blocked, vacated, or permanently stalled.
multiplier: 4 hits out of 10 cases = 40% base rate for surviving structural friction to final publication.
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act standards and general judicial review frameworks remain stable on this timescale.
